Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

Now let customers contact a business through its portal. They register with
`POST /api/v1/registrations`, for example
`{"user":{"name":"Avery","email":"avery@example.test","password":"my-customer-password"}}`.
They should use the existing verification, login, profile, and recovery flows.

A customer opens a request like this:

```http
POST /api/v1/requests

{"request":{"subject":"Cannot download my receipt","comment":{"body":"The download button does nothing."}}}
```

Return it inside `request`, with its ID, subject, status, requester ID, and timestamps. A new
request is open. Customers can list their own requests, open one, and read its comments at
`/requests`, `/requests/:id`, and `/requests/:id/comments`. Staff have the corresponding `/tickets`
routes; return records inside `ticket` there and include the requester as `{"id":10,"name":"Avery","email":"avery@example.test"}`.
Lists use the plural resource name. Comments include their body, author (`id` and `name`), whether
they're `public`, and when they were created.

Replies go through PATCH. For example, the owner can answer and mark a ticket pending:

```http
PATCH /api/v1/tickets/42

{"ticket":{"comment":{"body":"Please try again now."},"status":"pending"}}
```

Customers reply through `/requests/:id` with the `request` envelope. Customer replies reopen pending
or solved requests unless they mark the request solved in the same update. Staff can choose open, pending,
or solved. Posting a staff reply by itself doesn't change the status.

Paginate lists with `page` and `per_page` (default 1 and 25), returning `count`, `page`, `per_page`,
`next_page`, and `previous_page` alongside the records. Show recently active tickets and requests
first, and comments oldest first. This is a portal-only conversation for now; replies don't send email.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Helpdesk API

Rails 8.1 API-only backend for the helpdesk SaaS. The frontend is a separate app.
All endpoints live under `/api/v1` and speak JSON.

## Setup

Requires Ruby 4.0 (see `.ruby-version`) and PostgreSQL. `DATABASE_URL` configures the
primary connection, for example:

    export DATABASE_URL="postgresql:///helpdesk_development?host=/var/lib/postgresql"
    bundle install
    bin/rails db:prepare
    bin/rails server            # Puma, on $PORT (default 3000)

Tests run against a separate database derived from `DATABASE_URL` (`helpdesk_development`
becomes `helpdesk_test`), or against `TEST_DATABASE_URL` if it is set:

    bin/rails test

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | none | PostgreSQL connection |
| `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL` | `http://localhost:3001` | Base URL for verification and reset links. Also the only browser origin allowed by CORS. |
| `HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM` | `support@example.test` | Sender address for outgoing email |
| `SMTP_ADDRESS`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `localhost`, `587`, none, none | SMTP delivery (production). Development writes mail to `tmp/mails/`. |
| `SECRET_KEY_BASE` | none | Required by Rails in production, even though the API does not use cookies. |

## Conventions

- **Business header:** every endpoint except `POST /api/v1/account/create` needs
  `X-Helpdesk-Account: <subdomain>`. The header selects the business, and a session token only works within the business that issued it.
- **Sessions:** send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **Errors:** `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "details": {...}}}`. Common codes:
  `account_required` (400), `parameter_missing` (400), `invalid_json` (400), `unauthorized` (401),
  `invalid_credentials` (401), `email_not_verified` (403), `account_cancelled` (403), `forbidden` (403),
  `account_not_found` (404), `validation_failed` (422), `invalid_token` (422),
  `invalid_current_password` (422), `already_cancelled` / `not_cancelled` / `reactivation_expired` (422).
- **Timestamps** are ISO 8601 UTC. Record IDs are integers.

## Endpoints

| Method and path | Auth | Purpose | Success |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /account/create` | none | Register a business and its owner (admin). Sends a verification email. | 201 `{account, user, message}` |
| `GET /portal` | header | Public business name and subdomain. | 200 `{portal: {name, subdomain}}` |
| `POST /sessions` | header | Sign in. The email must be verified. | 201 `{session: {id, token}, user, account}` |
| `DELETE /session` | token | Sign out this session. | 204 |
| `GET /account` | token | Full account, including cancellation status. | 200 `{account}` |
| `POST /account/cancel` | owner | Cancel the business and revoke all its sessions. | 200 `{account}` |
| `POST /account/reactivate` | owner | Reactivate within 90 days of cancellation. | 200 `{account}` |
| `GET /me` | token | Current user. | 200 `{user}` |
| `PATCH /me` | token | Update the name: `{"user":{"name":"Jo Smith"}}`. | 200 `{user}` |
| `PUT /me/password` | token | `{"password_change":{"current_password":"...","password":"..."}}`. Signs out all sessions. | 200 `{message}` |
| `POST /email_verifications` | header | `{"email_verification":{"email":"..."}}`. Emails a new link, replacing the old one. | 202 |
| `POST /email_verifications/confirm` | header | `{"email_verification":{"token":"..."}}`. | 200 `{user}` |
| `POST /password_resets` | header | `{"password_reset":{"email":"..."}}`. Emails a new reset link, replacing the old one. | 202 |
| `POST /password_resets/confirm` | header | `{"password_reset":{"token":"...","password":"..."}}`. Signs out all sessions. | 200 `{message}` |

Email requests answer the same way whether or not the address is registered.

Links sent by email:

- `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/verify-email?account=<subdomain>&token=<token>`
- `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/reset-password?account=<subdomain>&token=<token>`

## Account lifecycle

- Only the owner (the admin who registered the business) can cancel or reactivate.

# Helpdesk API

Rails 8.1 API-only backend for the helpdesk SaaS. The frontend is a separate app.
All endpoints live under `/api/v1` and speak JSON.

## Setup

Requires Ruby 4.0 (see `.ruby-version`) and PostgreSQL. `DATABASE_URL` configures the
primary connection, for example:

    export DATABASE_URL="postgresql:///helpdesk_development?host=/var/lib/postgresql"
    bundle install
    bin/rails db:prepare
    bin/rails server            # Puma, on $PORT (default 3000)

Tests run against a separate database derived from `DATABASE_URL` (`helpdesk_development`
becomes `helpdesk_test`), or against `TEST_DATABASE_URL` if it is set:

    bin/rails test

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | none | PostgreSQL connection |
| `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL` | `http://localhost:3001` | Base URL for verification and reset links. Also the only browser origin allowed by CORS. |
| `HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM` | `support@example.test` | Sender address for outgoing email |
| `SMTP_ADDRESS`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `localhost`, `587`, none, none | SMTP delivery (production). Development writes mail to `tmp/mails/`. |
| `SECRET_KEY_BASE` | none | Required by Rails in production, even though the API does not use cookies. |

## Conventions

- **Business header:** every endpoint except `POST /api/v1/account/create` needs
  `X-Helpdesk-Account: <subdomain>`. The header selects the business, and a session token only works within the business that issued it.
- **Sessions:** send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

  `invalid_credentials` (401), `email_not_verified` (403), `account_cancelled` (403), `forbidden` (403),

  `invalid_current_password` (422), `already_cancelled` / `not_cancelled` / `reactivation_expired` (422).
- **Timestamps** are ISO 8601 UTC. Record IDs are integers.

| Method and path | Auth | Purpose | Success |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /account/create` | none | Register a business and its owner (admin). Sends a verification email. | 201 `{account, user, message}` |

  # Requests from any other origin are still processed, but get no CORS headers,

end

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH = 255

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  has_many :comments, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, inverse_of: :ticket, dependent: :destroy

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: {maximum: SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH}
  validates :status, inclusion: {in: STATUSES}

  # Most recently active first. Every comment and status change touches updated_at.
  scope :recent_first, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Opens a request for `requester` with its first comment. Both are saved, or neither is.
  def self.open!(requester:, subject:, body:)
    ticket = new(account: requester.account, requester:, subject:, status: "open")
    ticket.comments.build(author: requester, body:, public: true)
    ticket.save!
    ticket
  end

  # A customer's update: an optional public reply, optionally marking the request solved.
  # A reply reopens a pending or solved request, unless the same update marks it solved.
  def requester_update!(author:, comment: nil, solve: false)
    transaction do
      comments.create!(author:, body: comment[:body], public: true) if comment.present?
      update!(status: solve ? "solved" : "open") if comment.present? || solve
    end
  end

  # A staff update: an optional reply (public unless marked private), and an optional status.
  # A reply alone never changes the status.
  def staff_update!(author:, comment: nil, status: nil)
    transaction do
      if comment.present?
        comments.create!(author:, body: comment[:body], public: comment.fetch(:public, true))
      end
      update!(status:) unless status.nil?
    end
  end
end

# Offset pagination for list endpoints: `?page=2&per_page=10`. Defaults are page 1 and 25 per page.
# per_page is capped at MAX_PER_PAGE. Values that are not positive whole numbers are rejected.
module Paginatable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_PAGE = 1
  DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25
  MAX_PER_PAGE = 100

  class InvalidPagination < StandardError
    attr_reader :param

    def initialize(param)
      @param = param
      super("#{param} must be a positive whole number.")
    end
  end

  included do
    rescue_from InvalidPagination do |error|
      render_error(422, "validation_failed", error.message, details: {error.param => ["must be a positive whole number"]})
    end
  end

  private

  # Renders one page of `scope` under `key`, with the paging fields alongside the records.
  # The block turns each record into its JSON.
  def render_page(key, scope)
    page = pagination_number(:page, DEFAULT_PAGE)
    per_page = [pagination_number(:per_page, DEFAULT_PER_PAGE), MAX_PER_PAGE].min

    count = scope.count
    records = scope.offset((page - 1) * per_page).limit(per_page)

    render json: {
      key => records.map { |record| yield record },
      count:,
      page:,
      per_page:,
      next_page: (page * per_page < count ? page + 1 : nil),
      previous_page: (page > 1 ? page - 1 : nil)
    }
  end

  def pagination_number(name, default)
    raw = params[name]
    return default if raw.blank?
    raise InvalidPagination, name unless raw.is_a?(String) && raw.match?(/\A[1-9]\d{0,8}\z/)

    raw.to_i
  end
end

(the total across all pages), `page`, `per_page`, `next_page`, and `previous_page`. The last two are `null`

Customers can now register through a portal, open requests, read and reply to them, and staff can work them through `/tickets`. The full suite passes (115 tests, including 54 new ones), and I also ran the whole flow over HTTP against Puma. The changes are uncommitted in `/app`.

**What's in place**
- **Registration:** `POST /api/v1/registrations` creates an unverified `customer` user and emails a verification link. The existing verification, sign-in, profile, and password-reset flows work for these users unchanged.
- **Customer routes:** `/requests` (list, create, show, reply via PATCH) and `/requests/:id/comments`. Customers only see their own requests, and an unknown or foreign request returns 404.
- **Staff routes:** `/tickets` (list, show, reply and/or set status via PATCH) and `/tickets/:id/comments`. Non-staff users get 403.
- **Status rules:** a customer reply reopens a pending or solved request unless the same update marks it solved. Customers can only set `solved`. Staff can set any of the three statuses, and a staff reply alone leaves the status alone.
- **Lists:** paginated with `page` and `per_page`, returning `count`, `page`, `per_page`, `next_page`, and `previous_page`. Requests and tickets are ordered by last activity, and comments are oldest first.
- **Persistence:** new `tickets` and `comments` tables. The dev database is migrated, and the business I used for the end-to-end check has been removed.

**Decisions to review**
- **Duplicate emails return 422** with "has already been taken" when that address is already registered in the same portal. This reveals that the address has an account there, unlike the verification and reset endpoints, which answer the same way either way. If you want that uniform behavior here too, it's a small change.
- **Opening a request requires a comment body** as well as a subject.
- **Private notes:** the spec mentions a `public` flag but not how to set it. I added `"public": false` on staff replies for internal notes. Customers never see them.
- **Pagination:** a `page` or `per_page` that isn't a positive whole number returns 422, and `per_page` is capped at 100.
- **Shared change:** I changed the `envelope` helper in `ApplicationController`. It used to drop a field of the wrong shape silently, so `"comment": "text"` would change the status and discard the reply. It now returns 422 naming the field. This also applies to existing endpoints, but only for malformed input.

**Not covered:** the spec's rule that replies don't send email is respected, but I didn't add a way to create agents or for staff to open tickets. There are also no status or search filters on the lists.
